Italy's most famous building is only standing because a war stopped people from finishing it.
It's eleven seventy-three, and the town of Pisa is rich, proud, and building the most beautiful bell tower in the world!
The builders finish the ground floor.
Halfway up the second floor, the foreman puts down his hammer...
Its foundation is only three meters deep, sitting on soft, wet clay.
And before anyone can fix it, Pisa goes to war,
and the builders walk off the job for almost a hundred years.
When their grandkids finally come back, they have a genius plan:
build the new floors taller on the short side.
Unluckily, now it's leaning, and bent like a banana.
You see, the ground under Pisa is like an old mattress.
Ever sat on the edge of one?
The side with your weight sinks, and the more it sinks, the more weight slides onto it.
That hundred-year war break gave the clay time to squeeze out its water and firm up.
Without it, the extra floors would have pushed the tower straight over.
By nineteen ninety, it was leaning so far that Italy closed it,
and engineers spent eleven years sneaking dirt out from under the high side.
They straightened it by forty-five centimeters...
Because a tower that stands up straight... is just a tower.
